comments.author: @replayeatsyoutube
comments.text:
I had a two great experiences with Carvana.
1st know the exact car make model, year and color you are shopping for. Research so you know the trim and the accessories that were originally offered.
2nd before setting up a delivery date, schedule an appointment with a mechanic/ and your car shop for a complete inspection. I mean complete. It might cost you $200.
3 get the car inspected by the mechanic within 7 days. If the mechanic finds issues, you call and arrange for a pick up and return. Carvana has a 7 day no questions ask policy. The 7 days starts on the delivery day which is counted as 1
4 No reason to purchase a car with 100,000 miles already on it. Our cars were both at or below 50,000 miles on the odometer. Low mileage cars are still available as a large population of people worked from home and remote during 2020-2023, where daily driving was not necessary.
5 I purchased a 2016 Toyota Corolla and my sister in law purchased a 2018 Toyota Camry - we followed the above steps for each and no problems, its been over two years. Carvana provides carfax and experian reports, for each vehicle. Review those for any potential problems like where mileage doesn't make sense or there are missed yearly emissions smog testing and state mandatory inspections. You will quickly notice how often the previous owner got oil changes. 5K mile oil change interval is ideal, anything more than that you are rolling the dice especially if its a turbo engine. You will quickly learn what is and what's not a clean and well maintained car from these reports. Stay away from multi owner cars and those that have had an accident, no matter how minor it is described. Target one previous owner no accident cars from the carfax and experian reports. And no cars listed as being used in a rental agency.
6 Do your research on where the car is coming from. You should avoid purchasing a car from California around Dec 2025 or those put on sale a few months after that date. There was massive flooding in CA and you don't want to buy a flooded car that has been cleaned up and detailed. Do the same research for other states for example for tornado or hail damage. Texas, Arizona, Oregon, Nevada, WA state cars would be best for non rusty cars.
7 both carvana and carmax show high definition detailed pictures of the exterior the interior and engine bay area. I am lucky I have a great friend who had a past job in auto body. He was able to notice mismatching body panel gaps and over spray paint areas from previous accidents that I would have never picked up, just from the pictures. Original glass on cars have the non removable manufacturer label on the glass corner. If the label is missing, means the glass has been replaced which would be a sign of an accident or break in. Exception perhaps would be the windshield which often gets rock damage and is replaced.
8 I would never buy a high end Mercedes, Porsche, BMW, Corvette, Lexus ....etc from carvana, carmax any other online site. You should get those as Dealer inspected used preowned and with some kind of warranty. Just my opinion.
9 With Carvana and Carmax, sign up for email or text alerts for your search criteria. Remember there are thousands of buyers looking for the same thing you want. 
10 And Lastly if the deal looks too good to be true it is. Walk away. Generally with Carvana and Carmax, you will lose the transportation and shipping fees if you return the car within the 7 day window but that is a lot better than buying someone else's lemon. Yes you will pay for transportation and shipping fees for the car to be delivered to you as in carvana or to the sale location for carmax.
11 After a few weeks of viewing the sold cars and sale prices and condition of the vehicle you will start noticing the desired cars from the junk. The desired cars are gobbled up within hours. If your smart phone goes off with a Carvana alert get to your computer fast ! Once you get the car and decide to keep it, the car will be provided with a temp plate/ car window document valid for 30 days providing ample time to visit your DMV for permanent plates. Few weeks after registration with your State the title arrives in the mail that was our experience with carvana..
12 I know both carvana and carmax offer financing and trade ins, but I have not dealt with those services so I have nothing to comment.
13 Drive your car to the local Police Dept or Sheriff office and ask for a K9 walk through for any drugs or paraphernalia. That way it can be documented and disposed of, if something is detected and found by the K9. For us it was a free service and the Sheriff said he wished every used car owner would do this as it gives the K9s real life experience and best for you to find it now and not be surprised during a traffic stop.

comments.author: @sintiasmare6561
comments.text: People need to understand a car is a big investment with little to no return cause of depreciation. Sure some cars value might still remain good but you lose when investing in a car. When shopping for a car, people need to research that certain car they're getting. Look on Google and YouTube for information. You have to search for the best and worst years of that specific model. Gotta search for common issues on that car and decide if that's something you'd be willing to handle. People need to stick with brands that are reputable brands (Toyota, Honda, Mazda etc...NO Hyundai or Kia). I've never bought a car from any of those companies but it is convenient to do all the transactions over your phone. Majority of the cars sold to those companies are headaches that people just wanted to get rid of. If anything I'd probably shoot for a reputable brand with 75k miles or less cause I know it'll have less to no issues. Only problem tho is for example those companies will sell a used Toyota Corolla for the same price as a new one. In that case it's better to get brand new even if it cost $2-3k more. Sometimes you'll even get a 0% interest rate, full warranty and you'll be the first owner. Out of carvana and CarMax, you'd probably have a better chance of getting a reliable ride going to enterprise car sales and getting a used rental car. Prices are basically the same, the cars usually have 30-50k miles on them cause thats when enterprise takes them out the fleet. They might still come with a factory warranty but even if they don't, you can get an extended warranty from that brand dealership. Plus enterprise actually services their cars. I use to work at a national tire shop where I use to service their rentals. Most people don't even do their oil changes on time. Sure they get driven hard but no harder than what people do in their personal cars. I've sold 1 car to CarMax back during COVID and I got a fair deal for my car but I never bought a car from them. If you're mechanically inclined and know a thing or two about cars like I am, you're more likely to know which brands and models to get and what not to get. The only brands I would get is Toyota, Honda, Mazda, Lexus, Acura and even Mitsubishi. I'm not a fan of Mitsubishi cause they're in bed with Nissan but they're CVTs are tuned differently than Nissan. Only Nissan I'd mess with is the frontier. As far as cars, I prefer naturallly aspirated engines over turbos. I prefer regular transmissions over CVT. I don't care for all the bells and whistles newer cars come with but unfortunately they come with it, so I prefer the base trim levels. Any domestic car I won't get. I own a 2008 Ford crown victoria P71 and even tho it's a Ford, their cars from the early 2000s and before including other domestic brands were pretty solid. My specific model was like the Toyota of Ford. She currently has 256k and still going strong. Bought her in 2018 for $1300. Honestly if you're gonna go used, go with an older model vehicle before 2010. You'll be better off than gambling with newer model cars and dealing with the BS of carvana and CarMax. Paying cash for cars is much better than even financing. Overall, people just gotta do they're research instead of getting something cause it looks cool or cute.
